title: introduce-credential-pipeline-and-stream-aux-interfaces-across-sdks
author: Evan Thompson
description: Summary: Add a cross-language 'credential pipeline' abstraction and lightweight 'stream aux' interfaces to improve streaming ergonomics and parity across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Motivation: multiple SDKs had slightly divergent auth lifecycles and ad-hoc small-stream helpers (progress events, sideband diagnostic frames). This PR centralizes the retry hints and TTL-aware credential handoff semantics into a small, well-documented pipeline and introduces an optional StreamAux interface for low-bandwidth side channels. The goal is ergonomics parity (same mental model across languages), clearer retry semantics when credentials refresh mid-stream, and a minimal surface for telemetry. What this does: 1) Core: introduce credential pipeline primitives (CredProvider, CredLease, RenewHint) and a deterministic retry predicate that SDKs can opt into. 2) Streaming: add StreamAux interface (send_event, on_progress, annotate_chunk) for small opaque metadata frames and a typed wire envelope recommendation. 3) SDK adapters: Python/TS/Go adapters and examples that demonstrate session handoff, zero-downtime token swap, and retry profile hints for transient 401/5xx scenarios. 4) Version bumps: prepares packaging metadata for redwood-sdk-python v1.27.0, redwood-sdk-typescript v1.31.2, redwood-sdk-go v1.12.4 with compatibility notes. 5) Telemetry: report cred lifecycle events (lease_acquired, lease_renew, fallback_used) to existing telemetry hooks. Migration notes: existing SDKs keep current APIs but gain opt-in constructors (credential_pipeline=...) and optional stream_aux argument on streaming endpoints. Recommended upgrade path: enable pipeline in staging, exercise long-running streams with forced token rotation, then flip in production. Testing: unit tests for the pipeline state machine, integration test with a simulated token server, and a small cross-SDK example app under examples/cred-lease-demo. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (internal doc ENG-4981) - [x] adapters for Python/TS/Go included - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs and examples added - [x] version bumps prepared - [x] changelog entry

review_comments: Aisha Patel: This is a solid API surface. Two asks: 1) can we make the RenewHint pluggable so integrators can provide custom clock skew adjustments? 2) tests should include a simulated intermittent auth server to validate backoff behavior.
Evan Thompson: Thanks — made RenewHint configurable (clock_skew_adjust) and added intermittent auth server in integration tests. See commit feat(test): intermittent-auth-integration (4th) above.
Marcus Li: The StreamAux API looks good but we should be explicit about ordering guarantees for on_progress vs main data frames. Can we add a small section in the wire envelope doc?

Evan Thompson: Added a wire envelope appendix and a deterministic ordering guarantee for auxiliary frames: auxiliary frames are best-effort and ordered per-connection; consumers must be resilient to dropped aux frames.
Sofia García: CI failed on first run (flake in ts test). Re-ran CI and all checks passed. LGTM after CI green.
Marcus Li: Approved after minor doc clarifications.
Aisha Patel: Approved. Please squash-merge with a concise commit message referencing ENG-4981/ENG-5004.
